partner_result.application: Applied at the actual four-coordinate inequality for every leaking outside coordinate j and combined by a minimum with the new collective leakage bound.

supporting_source.application: Used after exact completion of the protected indefinite pair; the residual is Xi[beta+2a^T V]+R(V), with R arbitrarily correlated with the slope.

new_results.statement: For an indefinite rank-two physical triple with nonzero singular values nu1>=nu2 and unit kernel k, L=||A[S^c,S]k||2>0 implies ||p||inf <= 8(3/2)^(1/4)/sqrt(nu2 L)+2sqrt(3)/sqrt(nu1nu2), uniformly over arbitrary outside curvature, translations, unbounded supports and fragments.
Choosing the largest kernel coordinate i and completing the remaining 2x2 principal pair gives A[S^c,S]k=k_i(g-F^T C^-1 b), so the full kernel leakage is exactly a whole-bank random slope.

target_valid_application: For B=diag(1,-1,0) with diffuse bank leakage w_m=m^-1/2(1,...,1), the full spectrum is {1,-1,1,-1,0,...}; the new bound is 8*2^(-1/4)+2<8.728 uniformly in m, while the partner single-coordinate inequality scales like C4 sqrt(m).
unresolved_implication: From bare s3(A)>=1 in each surviving N3/no-pivot state, force either a rank-two indefinite physical triple with controlled nu2 L and nu1nu2, an existing volume/ridge/cross-bank/mixed-hub exit, or a product-safe outside-curvature branch.
next_step: Splice the collective rank-two leakage gate into the current mixed-hub/no-pivot structural case tree and test whether small aggregate kernel leakage forces a quantitative outside-Schur curvature resource rather than selecting a small coordinate.
